label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 13 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: money-unit
case.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

rerun_command: python -m klaxon.evaluation run --model claude-opus-5-5 --cases money-unit --seeds 7 --steps 10 --tool-calls 8 --rate 3 --loop multi

expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 17:05:31Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It now sends our cent amounts to fake-provider as dollars, so the provider charges 100x what we record. For example, pmt_000230 is stored as 1291 cents, and pay_000230 was charged 129100. payments_match_provider flags every payment made since the redeploy: 56 findings at the alert, 77 at 17:05:57Z. pmt_000233 shows the same fault in another form. payments-api got HTTP 500s and left it pending, the provider charged 393000, and payment-confirmer refused the webhook because the amounts differ. ledger-consumer books provider events, so the ledger matches the inflated provider totals. Open points: no request body shows the amount sent, so the unit change is inferred from the exact 100x ratio and the timing. The 500s for pmt_000233 are unexplained.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails with 77 findings at cutoff 17:05:57Z, up from 56 at the alert. Every sampled finding is a provider charge of exactly 100x our amount_cents, starting at pmt_000230. pmt_000233 is pending but was charged 393000 cents. The other 4 invariants pass. matches_provider shows the ledger and the provider both at $387,924.24, so the ledger booked the inflated amounts.
payments-api was redeployed at 17:05:31Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It is the only container created after the 17:04:04Z stack start.
pmt_000229 succeeded at 17:05:30.814Z, just before the redeploy, with 1708 cents. It is not among the sampled findings.
pmt_000230, the first finding, succeeded at 17:05:32.582Z, just after the redeploy. Our side logged amount_cents 1291.
The pmt_000230 trace: payments-api inserts the payment as pending, POSTs to fake-provider /v1/payments (HTTP 200), and updates the payment. The span does not record the amount sent.
For pmt_000233, payments-api logged three errors between 17:05:33.377Z and 17:05:37.633Z, each '/v1/payments failed after 3 attempts: HTTP 500', and left the payment pending.
At 17:05:32.774Z, before the first payments-api error, payment-confirmer refused evt_000254 (payment.succeeded, pay_000233). The provider amount was 393000 cents and ours is 3930.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 17:05:31Z deploy, which should restore the cents unit. Then run the money check and confirm that new payments match the provider. The rollback repairs nothing already done. A separate data repair, reviewed by a human, must refund or adjust the 100x overcharges for every affected payment (pmt_000230 onward, 77+ findings). It must also correct the ledger entries that booked the inflated amounts and resolve pmt_000233, which is pending but charged. Check every finding for duplicate charges from the retried POSTs.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, and payment requests in that window fail or retry. The rollback also restores the earlier values of PROVIDER_BREAKER and REFUND_CONNECTION, if they changed in the same deploy. Money already charged and booked at 100x stays wrong until the data repair is done.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with its current settings (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned) or with corrected settings. Use the current settings only as a brief stopgap, because they cause the overcharging.
